facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man from eastern India presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue present for the last 4 months
The lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue, which gradually grew and subsequently ulcerated
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history includes well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue with a clean base and irregular and elevated heaped-up margins
No underlying induration, friability, or bleeding on manipulation
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils
Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
Special stains (Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver nitrate and periodic acid–Schiff) highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

concepts.why: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo and positive special stains for fungal forms are characteristic of histoplasmosis.
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo and positive special stains for fungal forms can also be seen in cryptococcosis.
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo and positive special stains for fungal forms are also consistent with blastomycosis.
The presence of a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue could be consistent with a chronic traumatic ulcer, although the absence of a history of trauma makes this less likely.
A nonhealing ulcer on the tongue could be a sign of squamous cell carcinoma, although the histopathological examination did not support this diagnosis.
